english.title: Falsely claiming excessive powers as designated National Crime Agency officer
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to deceive,

(A)_[made a statement,]_
(B)_[did an act,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE STATEMENT / ACT..), calculated falsely to suggest that you had powers as a designated National Crime Agency officer as defined by paragraph 30 of Schedule 5 to the Crime and Courts Act 2013, that exceeded the powers you actually had
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 23(1)(c) and (2) of Schedule 5 to the Crime and Courts Act 2013.

english.notes: Designated officer means the Director General or any other National Crime Agency officer if designated as having operational powers

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 51 weeks imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Note:
Until the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (alteration of penalties for summary offences) the reference to the period of 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to the period of 6 months.

Time limit on prosecutions:
Six months
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
